newsitem.title: USA: Camdessus won't comment on speculation on ECB job.
newsitem.headline: Camdessus won't comment on speculation on ECB job.

text.p: International Monetary Fund (IMF) head Michel Camdessus said on Thursday that talk that France might want him to head the future European Central Bank (ECB) was press speculation and declined further comment.

Newspapers have speculated that France might back Camdessus, a Frenchman, for the central bank job, over Dutch central bank head Wim Duisenberg, who takes over this year as head of the ECB's forerunner, the European Monetary Institute.
Asked about these reports, Camdessus told a news conference, "This is press speculation. The IMF does not like to feed speculation."
He has said previously he is happy in his current job as managing director of the IMF.
France has said it should not be a foregone conclusion that Duisenberg will become European Central Bank head, but has not suggested any rival candidates.
